facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s developed asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Six days later, he was hospitalized with diffuse bilateral pneumonia
Numerous 3- to 6-mm pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting were noted on the trunk
The papules were asymptomatic
Within 48 hours the papules evolved to an extensive, but not confluent, purpuric rash

Nasopharyngeal swab using real-time reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) - Diagnostic testing on superficial skin sample for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 viruses (all negative)
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses (negative)
RT-PCR testing of fixed skin tissue for SARS-CoV-2 (negative)
Histologic analysis showed: - Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis
Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels without fibrinoid necrosis or thrombosis

concepts.why: The patient's histologic analysis showed early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels.
The patient developed an extensive, but not confluent, purpuric rash within 48 hours of the initial papules.
The patient presented with pseudovesicular papules that evolved into a purpuric rash, consistent with a viral exanthem.
The patient was hospitalized with diffuse bilateral pneumonia.
The patient's histologic analysis showed extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis.
The patient's histologic analysis and clinical presentation are consistent with a vasculitic dermatosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Varicella-like rash due to other viral infections
concepts.why: The presence of large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration and negative immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses suggests a varicella-like rash due to another viral infection.

The combination of pseudovesicular papules, superficial crusting, and dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis is consistent with erythema multiforme.

rationales.F05: Purpuric rash is a key feature of vasculitis and vasculitic dermatosis
rationales.F09: Epidermal necrosis is a characteristic feature of certain skin conditions
rationales.F10: Multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration are seen in viral infections
rationales.F12: Early-stage vasculitic alterations are indicative of vasculitis

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including the evolution of papules to a purpuric rash and the histologic findings of extensive epidermal necrosis, acantholysis, and perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, are most consistent with Vasculitic Dermatosis, which explains the decisive findings without an unexplained strong contradiction.
